subject: Live chat backpressure incident — mitigation steps & post-incident actions
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@skyline.ai>, support@skyline.ai
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observed high latency on streaming chat (live session) — immediate mitigations

Hi Alice / Skyline team,

We observed elevated end-to-end latency for streaming chat sessions affecting a subset of your live user traffic starting ~09:05 PT. Users are seeing stalls in the stream payloads (long pauses between chunk deliveries) rather than request errors. Our telemetry shows increased backpressure on the live-response worker pool driven by a burst of long-horizon requests with high token churn.

Immediate actions we've taken: 
- Throttled burst concurrency on the affected shard to protect tail latency.
- Enabled short-term prefix KV cache retention for Skyline's project to reduce repeated compute.
- Temporarily routed new sessions to a compatible lower-cost model variant with similar behavior but shorter decoding windows.

Recommended customer-side mitigations (low friction):
1) Switch inbound clients to non-streaming (polling) for critical sessions while we stabilize.
2) Reduce max_tokens / set response_token_budget=256 for interactive flows.
3) Enable incremental result handling (process partial chunks) rather than waiting for final event.

I've attached a short runbook and a minimal client patch that implements a safe non-streaming fallback. We'll keep this thread updated with timeline and next steps.

— Mina
Lead Incident Manager, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.ai

Attachments: backpressure-runbook.pdf (runbook), client-fallback-sample.patch (diff)

From: Alice Chen <alice@skyline.ai>

Cc: support@skyline.ai
Date: 2027-04-02T09:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed high latency on streaming chat (live session) — immediate mitigations

Thanks Mina — we see the same stalls on our side and traffic for our main webchat is in active campaigns today. We're going to flip the clients to non-streaming for the highest-value cohorts. A couple quick questions: 
- How long do you expect the routing to the lower-cost variant to remain?
- Any suggested short changes to our retry/backoff to avoid duplicated user messages?

We'll test the sample patch now and report back in ~20m.

— Alice
Senior Product Manager, Skyline.ai
alice@skyline.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed high latency on streaming chat (live session) — immediate mitigations

Hi team — quick technical notes for Alice: 
- Lower-cost model routing is expected to remain for ~90 minutes while we drain the contention; we'll monitor and decide on returning traffic case-by-case.
- Client retry guidance: implement idempotent message ids and use exponential backoff starting at 300ms with jitter (avoid blind rapid retries).
- If you see partial-delivery artifacts, add a client-side prefix dedupe using the request id.

I'll follow up in an hour with an updated ETA and the initial telemetry snapshot.

— Neha
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-02T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed high latency on streaming chat (live session) — immediate mitigations

Update from our side: the non-streaming fallback patch applied to 3% of sessions looks good (no duplication, reduced perceived latency). We'll scale to 30% over the next 40 minutes. One user reported an out-of-order chunk when switching back to streaming; we rolled that session back and will capture logs.

Can Redwood confirm whether there's any residual risk of KV-cache eviction for our project while using the fallback routing?

— Alice

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@skyline.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps (short-term + postmortem plan)

Hi Alice — thanks for the rapid coordination and for testing the fallback. Quick summary of what we learned and next actions: 

What happened (short): 
- A sustained burst of long-horizon conversations from third-party traffic exhausted hot KV windows on one serving shard, causing worker backpressure and delayed chunk emission.

Customer impact: 
- Skyline: intermittent stalls for active webchat cohorts (affecting ~0.8% of sessions at peak).

Immediate remediation we executed: 
- Burst concurrency throttling on the shard; routing to a compatible model variant; increased prefix-KV retention for Skyline; recommended non-streaming fallback.

Client recommendations we validated: 
- Continue using non-streaming fallback for critical cohorts until we confirm full recovery.
- Ensure idempotent request ids and exponential backoff to prevent duplicate user messages.
- Reduce max_tokens to lower decode pressure for interactive sessions.

Next steps (timeline): 
- 2027-04-02 17:00 PT: Redwood runs a focused postmortem and identifies kernel-level pressure points (owner: Infra).
- 2027-04-04: Postmortem write-up and RCA shared (owner: Reliability + Applied ML).
- Follow-up: we will provide a small credit for the impacted hourly usage (outlined in a separate billing note) and schedule a 30-minute technical review with your engineering team.

Attached runbook and client patch are in the thread for your engineers. We'll also produce a short checklist for embedding a robust streaming fallback into your SDK (tentative link in related_links).

Thanks again for the fast action — we'll keep this thread as the canonical incident communication until the postmortem is published.

— Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai
